summary: A server-rendered Go web app with templ components and htmx, where forms validate on the server and pages update without a JavaScript build.
description: Start a Go web app that renders HTML on the server. templ turns typed components into Go code, run through go tool, and a check fails when the generated code is stale. htmx, downloaded once and embedded in the binary, swaps parts of the page. One notes page proves the shape: its form posts with htmx and gets back the new item, invalid input comes back as the form with inline errors and a 422, and the same form works as a plain post without JavaScript. Request logging, an error page, cross-site post protection and graceful shutdown are wired in, and tests assert on the rendered HTML. The recipe picks no database, sign-in or CSS framework.
seoDescription: A Go web app recipe with templ components, htmx partial updates, server-side form validation, HTML tests and graceful shutdown, with no Node toolchain.

projectExamples.title: Internal admin dashboard
projectExamples.description: Illustrative: replace the notes page with tables and edit forms for an internal team, keeping server-side validation and partial updates. A database and sign-in are work the project still has to add.

plain.whatItIs: A starter Go website where the server builds every page as HTML and a small script updates parts of the page, so there is no JavaScript build step.
goodAt: Forms and pages that check input on the server
Internal tools and dashboards kept in one Go program
Interactive pages without a separate frontend app
notGoodAt: Rich client-side apps that work offline; choose react-vite or react-router.
JSON APIs for other programs; choose go-api.
Projects that need a database or sign-in from the start; you add both yourself.
